title: C-06: codon use in the supplied reporter reference
question: How does the reference CDS compare with historical highly expressed yeast codon counts?
materials: G1: construct_reference.gbk; original project GenBank reference.
R1: yeast_codon_reference.cut; EMBOSS Eyeast_cai, 24 CDS, TranstermMay1994.
methods: Format only LOCUS metadata spacing in memory; verify ORIGIN bases and raw-file hashes are unchanged. Extract the labelled CDS and translate with standard nuclear code 1; record adjacent stop separately.
Derive weights from integer counts within full synonymous families; replace true zeros by 0.5; exclude Met, Trp and stops from CAI. Sensitivity: zero = 1.
Compare whole CDS and first 50 codons; measure GC by position and flag low-weight clusters and A/T homopolymers.
results: The labelled CDS spans reference bases 748-2097: 1350 nt and 450 aa; its translation matches its annotation.
The adjacent triplet is TAA; a start-to-adjacent-stop segment has 1353 nt.
Count-derived yeast-reference CAI is 0.1708, versus 0.1495 in the first 50 codons; zero = 1 gives 0.1764.
There are 185/450 low-weight codons and 40 consecutive stretches of at least 2 codons; GC is 40.37% and GC3 is 35.78%.
conclusion: The 1350-nt reporter CDS encodes 450 amino acids and matches its annotated translation. Its yeast-reference CAI is 0.1708, compared with 0.1495 in the first 50 codons. There are 185 low-weight codon positions and 40 consecutive stretches of at least 2 codons, locating regions for a synonymous-redesign comparison.

figures.caption: G1 CDS weights and CAI using R1 integer counts. CAI excludes Met/Trp; zero counts replaced by 0.5, with zero = 1 sensitivity. Cutoff 0.2 is descriptive. One reference sequence; no biological error bars.
GC percentage in G1 overall and by codon position. One deterministic reference sequence; no biological error bars.

scope_and_assumptions: The supplied GenBank reference is the analysis sequence. Codon weights use integer counts from the historical 24-CDS yeast table, with the stated zero-count convention. This sequence-level comparison covers coding integrity and codon composition; tested-clone identity, strain-specific expression, transcript context and cadmium performance are outside its scope.
